8	# ADR-005: Power-Based Routing Replaces `model_routes`
9	
10	## Superseded in part by ADR-009
11	
12	ADR-009 owns the v0.11 public routing surface. The power-routing mechanics in
13	this ADR remain implementation reference, but profile, target, alias, and
14	surface-policy vocabulary here is historical.
15	
16	| Date | Status | Deciders | Related | Confidence |
17	|------|--------|----------|---------|------------|
18	| 2026-04-25 | Proposed | Fizeau maintainers | `CONTRACT-003`, `SD-005`, `FEAT-004` | Medium |
19	
20	## Context
21	
22	SD-005 currently makes `model_routes:` the resolution surface: users
23	hand-author ordered candidate lists in YAML, the CLI re-reads them and
24	synthesizes a `RouteDecision` injected through
25	`ServiceExecuteRequest.PreResolved`, and the service treats that injected
26	decision as authoritative. The block exists to coordinate same-strength
27	failover among local LM Studio hosts and to keep the routing engine from
28	stripping configured candidates whose discovery probe is failing.
29	
30	That design creates two problems:
31	
32	1. **Configurable failover in user YAML is the wrong surface.** Provider source
33	   config should declare transport and auth. The model catalog should own model
34	   metadata and policy. The routing engine should build live candidates by
35	   joining discovered inventory with catalog data. Requiring users to also
36	   maintain `model_routes:` forces them to coordinate three sources of truth.
37	2. **The CLI synthesis path is leaky.** `cmd/agent/main.go:474-487` builds a
38	   `RouteDecision{Reason: "cli configured route"}`, threads it through
39	   `ServiceExecuteRequest.PreResolved`, and overwrites the request's
40	   `Provider`/`Model`/`Harness` fields, even though the contract says
41	   `PreResolved` mode ignores those fields. The mechanism exists only because
42	   the routing engine strips configured candidates on probe failure.
43	
44	The target shape is automatic routing: users configure provider sources and
45	endpoints, the agent asks those sources which models they can serve, joins the
46	inventory with the catalog, tracks service-observed usage and availability, and
47	selects the best candidate that satisfies the caller's hard constraints and
48	optional power bounds. Users do not maintain routing tables.
49	
50	## Decision
51	
52	Replace the `model_routes`-driven resolution surface with deterministic
53	power-based routing.
54	
55	### Power-Driven Candidate Inventory
56	
57	The primary routing strength input is numeric model `power`, an integer from
58	1..10 owned by the catalog. Higher means more capable for agent tasks. `0`
59	means unknown, missing, or not eligible for automatic routing. The routing
60	contract is numeric: request fields are `MinPower` and `MaxPower`
61	(`--min-power` / `--max-power` in CLI form).
62	
63	The service must build a complete joined inventory before choosing:
64	
65	1. **Provider source and harness inventory** — enumerate every available
66	   execution surface: prepaid subscription harnesses, native provider sources,
67	   configured endpoints, and test harnesses only when explicitly requested.
68	2. **Model inventory** — ask each surface what concrete models it can serve.
69	   Live `/models` or harness discovery output wins. Configured endpoint default
70	   models are fallback hints, not the whole inventory.
71	3. **Catalog join** — match discovered concrete models to catalog entries.
72	   Catalog metadata supplies family, context window, reasoning support, tool
73	   support, quality benchmarks, deprecation status, list price,
74	   provider/deployment class, and required `power`. Discovered models without
75	   catalog power remain inspectable and may be used when explicitly pinned, but
76	   they are not eligible for automatic routing.
77	4. **Usage/cost join** — attach live usage/quota signals where the surface can
78	   provide them. Prepaid harnesses expose quota remaining and reset time; paid
79	   metered providers expose static or live cost; local/free providers expose
80	   zero marginal cost plus measured latency/reliability when known.
81	5. **Inspectable output** — expose the joined inventory through
82	   `fiz --list-models` and the service `ListModels` API. Operators must
83	   be able to inspect the same candidate table the router scores: harness,
84	   provider source, endpoint/host, model, power, family,
85	   provider/deployment class, marginal cost, quota/reset, context, tool
86	   support, reasoning support, health, recent latency, availability status,
87	   auto-routable status, exact-pin-only status, and filter reasons.
88	
89	Power is a catalog-owned ordering. The catalog must assign power to every
90	model eligible for automatic routing. Initial values can be synthesized from
91	normalized coding benchmarks, context window, tool/reasoning support, recency,
92	cost, and provider/deployment class. Cost times recency is the default proxy
93	when benchmark data is sparse: within a provider/model family, the newest and
94	most expensive model is assumed to be that provider's strongest model unless
95	the catalog contains an explicit power/cost override. Older models in the same
96	family are not eligible for automatic routing unless the caller directly pins
97	them or the catalog records why their cost/power tradeoff is still useful.
98	
99	Provider/deployment class is part of power assignment. A local, community, or
100	self-hosted copy must not receive the same power as a managed cloud frontier
101	model solely because one benchmark is high. The catalog should keep raw inputs
102	and derived power together so new benchmark data can revise power
103	quantitatively instead of relying on hand-guessed membership buckets.
104	
105	Implementation status as of 2026-04-30: the embedded v4 catalog does not yet
106	define `power`, and `UpdateManifestPricing` only imports OpenRouter pricing and
107	context length. Adding catalog power schema and bootstrapping values for every
108	auto-routable model is prerequisite work before this routing interface can
109	ship.
110	
111	### Scoring
112	
113	Selection is a transparent utility calculation, not a hidden preference:
114	
115	```text
116	score = power_weighted_capability
117	      + latency_weight
118	      + placement_bonus
119	      + quota_bonus
120	      - marginal_cost_penalty
121	      - availability_penalty
122	      - stale_signal_penalty
123	```
124	
125	Prepaid quota changes the marginal-cost term. If a prepaid frontier harness has
126	healthy quota with a near reset, the effective marginal cost can be close to
127	zero and the highest-power model may rank first. If the same quota is
128	exhausted, stale, or far from reset, the quota bonus disappears and
129	cost/availability penalties apply. Local LM Studio, oMLX, Ollama, Lucebox,
130	vLLM, and llama-server providers are treated as free marginal cost but still
131	compete on capability, tool support, context, latency, availability, and
132	endpoint utilization when choosing among equivalent local endpoints.
133	
134	When no hard axes or power bounds are supplied, the service selects the best
135	lowest-cost viable auto-routable model it can use from the discovered
136	inventory. If strong prepaid quota is available and inexpensive at the margin,
137	the selected model may be a current frontier model. If only local providers are
138	live, the selected model may be a local model that clears capability gates.
139	
140	Provider placement is candidate-level. The native `agent` harness is not
141	itself local/free, prepaid, or metered; its child provider endpoints are. A
142	single native harness may contain local oMLX, local LM Studio, and paid
143	OpenRouter providers, and placement filtering must operate on those provider
144	candidates.
145	
146	Profile and target resolution remains catalog-owned, but provider-backed
147	routing must not stop at the target's primary concrete model when a target has
148	an ordered `candidates` list. For endpoints that publish live model discovery,
149	the router checks the ordered catalog candidates against the endpoint's
150	advertised model IDs and uses the first candidate that matches. This preserves
151	catalog tier policy while allowing local endpoints to serve provider-native
152	variants such as `Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit` when the primary candidate for the tier
153	is hosted somewhere else.
154	
155	Local endpoint routing adds a sticky utilization step inside the eligible
156	candidate set. If a request carries a sticky route key, normally the validated
157	`CorrelationID` or a future worker/session sequence ID, and that key has a live
158	lease for an endpoint that still serves the resolved model, the router reuses
159	that endpoint. If no valid lease exists, the router assigns the key to the
160	least-loaded equivalent endpoint. Existing sticky keys move only when the pinned
161	endpoint disappears, stops serving the model, enters cooldown, or crosses a hard
162	saturation threshold.
163	
164	Provider-owned utilization probes refine new sticky assignments but do not
165	replace route leases. `vllm` probes root `/metrics` for
166	`vllm:num_requests_running`, `vllm:num_requests_waiting`, and cache pressure.
167	`llama-server` probes root `/metrics` when started with `--metrics`, and falls
168	back to root `/slots` when metrics are unavailable. A configured
169	OpenAI-compatible base URL ending in `/v1` is converted to server root for these
170	probes. Probe failure makes utilization unknown/stale, not unavailable; routing
171	falls back to service-owned in-flight lease counts. In multi-machine
172	deployments, a shared lease backend is required for correct cross-process
173	stickiness and fair distribution because server metrics alone are sampled and
174	racy. The shared lease contract is specified in
175	[plan-2026-05-05-shared-lease-backend.md](../plan-2026-05-05-shared-lease-backend.md).
176	
177	### Hard Constraints
178	
179	`Execute` auto-fills only the axes the caller left unconstrained. `MinPower`
180	and `MaxPower` are broad routing policy. `Harness`, `Provider`, and exact model
181	identity are hard constraints:
182	
183	- `Harness=claude` means only the Claude harness may be used.
184	- `Provider=lmstudio` means only that provider source, or a clearly scoped
185	  endpoint selector on request surfaces that support endpoint selection, may be
186	  used.
187	- `Model=qwen-3.6-27b` means only that model identity may be used. The router
188	  may optimize provider source and endpoint choice inside that model
189	  constraint, but it must not select a different model.
190	
191	Catalog model aliases may resolve exact model identity or migration names, but
192	they do not define routing personas. If a constrained request cannot be
193	satisfied, routing fails with a detailed candidate/error trace instead of
194	broadening the constraint.
195	
196	Power bounds never override hard `--model`, provider-source/endpoint, or
197	`--harness` pins. Models with missing or zero power remain inspectable and may
198	be used by exact pin when available, but are excluded from unpinned automatic
199	routing.
200	
201	### Routing Decision
202	
203	Per request:
204	
205	1. **Build the candidate set** = every available `(harness, provider source,
206	   endpoint, model)` joined with the catalog and live provider/harness signals.
207	   Provider-backed profile/target references expand to the target's ordered
208	   catalog candidates before live discovery filtering.
209	2. **Apply hard constraints** before scoring: exact model identity, provider
210	   source/endpoint, harness, and any caller capability requirements.
211	3. **Filter by liveness** via `HealthCheck`, recent cooldown state, and live
212	   model discovery. Drop endpoints whose latest probe failed or which do not
213	   advertise the candidate model. If the filter empties the set, return a
214	   no-candidate decision with the full rejected trace.
215	4. **Filter by capability and power**: drop candidates whose context window <
216	   `EstimatedPromptTokens`, whose `SupportsTools()` is false when
217	   `RequiresTools` is true, whose reasoning support is below the request, whose
218	   catalog power is outside `MinPower`/`MaxPower`, or whose catalog status
219	   excludes automatic routing.
220	   Provider-native model IDs with unambiguous casing, prefix, quantization, or
221	   packaging differences must map back to catalog metadata before this gate, so
222	   discovered IDs inherit the intended power, context, tool-support, and
223	   auto-routable status.
224	5. **Apply sticky local endpoint assignment**: reuse an existing live lease for
225	   the sticky route key when present, otherwise use endpoint utilization and
226	   service-owned lease counts to choose among equivalent local endpoints serving
227	   the same resolved model.
228	6. **Score each survivor** using explicit score components: catalog quality,
229	   observed latency, marginal cost, quota/reset state, local/free preference
230	   when constraints are satisfied, endpoint utilization pressure, availability,
231	   and staleness penalties. Candidate trace output must expose these
232	   components.
233	7. **Dispatch top-1 once**, return the full ranked candidate trace in the
234	   routing decision event so callers can see why candidates 2..N lost.
235	8. **Report dispatch outcome** for the attempted candidate. Do not rotate to a
236	   second candidate. Record only availability/transport/protocol outcome facts
237	   for the attempted `(harness, provider source, endpoint, model)` tuple and
238	   return structured evidence to the caller.
239	
240	The implementation collapses these user-visible steps into two phases:
241	
242	**In `routing.Resolve` (`internal/routing/engine.go`):** consume a fully joined
243	candidate inventory, apply inline gates, score eligible candidates with power,
244	cost, latency, capability, availability, placement, and quota signals, then
245	rank and tie-break by cost and latency.
246	
247	**In `service.ResolveRoute` (`service_routing.go`):** call the engine once for
248	the requested power bounds/constraints and preserve the candidate trace even on
249	failure. Catalog power filtering happens in the engine's inline gates as part
250	of candidate construction. Retry is not performed here; the service returns the
251	ordered trace and attempted-route outcome for callers that own retry policy.
252	
253	### Caller-Owned Retry
254	
255	Retry is not an agent responsibility. `Execute` selects the best candidate,
256	dispatches that one candidate, and reports what happened. It does not try a
257	second candidate and it does not widen power bounds. Provider-specific
258	authentication, quota, transport, timeout, stream, subprocess, or protocol
259	failures are reported as facts about the attempted `(harness, provider source,
260	endpoint, model)` tuple; callers decide whether to issue a new request using a
261	different power range or different hard pins.
262	
263	Task-level escalation across power ranges is caller-owned. A caller such as
264	DDx owns that policy because it has task context, budget, retry limits, and
265	semantic evidence from tests/reviews. The service must therefore return enough
266	structured evidence for the caller to decide:
267	
268	- requested/effective power bounds and hard constraints
269	- selected candidate and full candidate trace with power and filter reasons
270	- attempted candidate and availability/transport failure class when dispatch
271	  failed
272	- score components and live cost/quota/latency facts
273	
274	The service exposes numeric power as machine-readable metadata, but it must not
275	present that metadata as a retry decision. The caller applies budgets, task
276	policy, and semantic evidence before issuing another request. If DDx later
277	determines from tests, review, or acceptance evidence that the chosen model was
278	too weak, DDx may retry the same task with a higher `MinPower` while preserving
279	first-attempt logs and budget accounting. DDx must not retry on deterministic
280	setup/config failures.
281	
282	### Provider Availability Feedback
283	
284	The agent service owns only provider availability feedback for candidate
285	selection. Minimum signal key: `(harness, provider source, endpoint, model)`.
286	A single bad endpoint must not poison its whole provider source, model family,
287	or power range.
288	
289	`Execute` records the attempted route's service-observed availability outcome:
290	success, transport errors, auth/quota/rate limits, 5xx responses, stream loss,
291	subprocess exit, timeout, malformed protocol output, capability mismatch,
292	duration, usage, and cost when known. The scoring engine uses availability,
293	latency, quota, and cooldown state from this store.
294	
295	Semantic task outcomes are not agent route feedback. If DDx learns that a model
296	was too weak because tests failed, review blocked, or acceptance criteria were
297	missed, that evidence belongs to DDx and may be contributed to the model
298	catalog or catalog-derived power ratings. It does not directly demote a live
299	provider in agent's transient routing state.
300	
301	### Subscription Quota Inputs
302	
303	Subscription harnesses already publish quota signals via harness caches
304	(`service_routing.go:335`). Cost ramping when at least 80% used already
305	exists. Keep both unchanged.
306	
307	OpenRouter and native HTTP providers do not publish live quota. Treat their
308	cost as static catalog cost in this round; file a follow-up bead for live-quota
309	plumbing on those providers but do not block this work on it.
310	
311	### `route-status` Redesigned
312	
313	Today `route-status` enumerates configured `model_routes` keys. Post-deletion
314	it must report eligible candidates for requested power bounds, with score
315	components (power, cost, latency, availability, filter reason) per candidate
316	and per-(provider source, model, endpoint) availability/latency facts.
317	Operators read it to answer "why did the router pick X?" rather than to
318	inspect their own YAML.
319	
320	### Delete
321	
322	- `model_routes:` config block; its loader in `internal/config/config.go`;
323	  `ServiceConfig.ModelRouteConfig`/`ModelRouteNames`.
324	- `service_routing.go` `model_routes` short-circuit landed in `90d9b03`
325	  (revert).
326	- `ServiceExecuteRequest.PreResolved` and `RouteDecision`-as-input.
327	  `PreResolved` was specified for a dry-run-then-execute flow that has no
328	  current consumer; its only producer in the repo is the CLI synthesis at
329	  `cmd/agent/main.go:474-487`, which is itself part of the `model_routes`
330	  deletion. `ResolveRoute` remains as a public method (operator dashboard /
331	  debug surface), but its result is informational, not re-injectable.
332	- CLI `selection.RouteCandidates` and `cmd/agent/routing_provider.go`
333	  provider-construction wrappers.
334	- SD-005 D4-D7 (`model_routes` surface). SD-005 rewritten from this ADR.
335	
336	### Keep
337	
338	- `routing.default_model`, `routing.default_model_ref`,
339	  `routing.health_cooldown` config keys. These are useful defaults, not
340	  `model_routes`.
341	- `internal/modelcatalog` as source of truth for cost, context, capability,
342	  power, provider/deployment class, and deprecation state.
343	- `internal/routing` engine scoring; refactor input source, do not rewrite
344	  scoring wholesale.
345	- Provider adapters, `internal/reasoning`, and the three session-log refactors
346	  landed earlier in this stack (`agent-7faa0edf`, `agent-b9bd700f`,
347	  `agent-99549438`).
348	- `--min-power`, `--max-power`, `--model`, `--provider`, `--reasoning`, and
349	  `--model-ref` CLI flags.
350	
351	## Consequences
352	
353	### Positive
354	
355	- One source of routing truth: provider source/endpoint config plus catalog
356	  metadata plus the engine's live inventory join.
357	- Local/free preference works automatically when local/free candidates satisfy
358	  requested power, tools, context, and availability constraints.
359	- Subscription harnesses can win when quota is healthy and effective marginal
360	  cost is low.
361	- Per-(provider source, endpoint, model) signal recovers from transient
362	  failures; one bad model or endpoint no longer locks out unrelated candidates.
363	- `RouteCandidate` exposes structured score components, not a free-form
364	  `Reason` string. Operator debugging gets a real surface.
365	- Public `RouteRequest` exposes the prompt-aware inputs the engine needs;
366	  service-side routing is no longer blind.
367	
368	### Negative
369	
370	- Removes a configurable failover surface. Operators who deliberately wire an
371	  ordered candidate list lose that knob. Mitigation: explicit provider
372	  source/endpoint and exact model pins remain; chaining failover by ordering
373	  candidates was already a workaround for the engine's probe-strip behavior,
374	  which this ADR fixes at the source.
375	- Public surface change to `RouteRequest`/`ServiceExecuteRequest` (new fields;
376	  one removed). Consumers re-bind.
377	- One-release deprecation window means operators with `model_routes:` configs
378	  do not get an immediate hard error. Acceptable trade-off vs. silent drift.
379	
380	## Migration
381	
382	Plan in three sharper beads (replacing the obsolete chain
383	`agent-9d120ece`/`6dd4ad97`/`873081a9`/`8804194f`, which is canceled with note
384	"superseded by ADR-005"):
385	
386	1. **Public surface update** — add `EstimatedPromptTokens` / `RequiresTools` to
387	   `RouteRequest` and `ServiceExecuteRequest`; remove
388	   `ServiceExecuteRequest.PreResolved`; add structured score components to
389	   `RouteCandidate`; update CONTRACT-003. Revert `90d9b03`. Update SD-005 with
390	   the auto-selection section and deprecation note.
391	2. **Wire inputs + scoring + route-status** — plumb new `RouteRequest` fields
392	   from CLI through `Execute`; wire engine gates against them; expose score
393	   components in routing-decision events; redesign `route-status` to show
394	   eligible candidates per intent. Add per-(provider source, endpoint, model)
395	   success/latency keying.
396	3. **Config + CLI cleanup + deprecation** — delete `model_routes` parser and
397	   `ServiceConfig.ModelRouteConfig`; delete CLI `selection.RouteCandidates`
398	   synthesis and `routing_provider.go` provider-construction wrappers; add
399	   deprecation warning when parsing legacy config; add boundary test forbidding
400	   `model_routes` re-entry.
401	
402	Step 1 blocks steps 2 and 3.
403	
404	## Out of Scope
405	
406	- Persistent EWMA across process restarts. In-memory + TTL is fine for this
407	  round; persistence + warm-start is its own design.
408	- ML-style prompt classification beyond `EstimatedPromptTokens`/`RequiresTools`.
409	  Ship deterministic power-based routing first.
410	- Live quota plumbing for OpenRouter and native HTTP providers. Static catalog
411	  cost suffices in this round.
412	- Reviewer pipeline overflow fixes, tracked separately in the upstream `ddx`
413	  repo.
414	
415	## Related
416	
417	- `CONTRACT-003` — public service surface; updated in step 1.
418	- `SD-005` — provider/model/routing config; rewritten from this ADR.
419	- `internal/routing/engine.go` — existing scoring engine; input source
420	  refactored, scoring retained.
421	- `service_routing.go` — subscription quota cost ramp stays; `90d9b03`
422	  short-circuit reverts.
